summary: Passkey (WebAuthn) assertions failing for CLI -> SSH bastion after IdP credential rotation
description:
Issue summary: Several engineers are unable to use FIDO2 passkeys (WebAuthn) to authenticate via the internal CLI which performs an Okta-backed SSO + device assertion flow before handing off to the ssh-gateway/bastion. The failures began shortly after the IdP (Okta) rotated a signing key and an internal token-rotation job ran overnight. Impact: blocked SSH access for 7 engineers across infra and platform teams; oncall runbooks cannot be executed; manual bastion access workaround is time-consuming and error-prone. Environment: prod us-west (ssh-gateway cluster behind auth-proxy), affected accounts are Redwood employees in engineering groups.

Expected behavior: CLI SSO flow should accept WebAuthn assertions and exchange the id_token for an ephemeral SSH session token.

Observed behavior: The CLI fails at the "device assertion" verification step with a cryptic error: "webauthn: assertion signature invalid (timestamp skew)" and the user is dropped back to interactive login. Manual browser SSO (console access) works for those users.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use the latest internal CLI (v2.14.0) and run `redwood ssh bastion --profile infra-usw2`
2) When prompted, complete WebAuthn passkey flow on device (Touch ID / YubiKey)
3) Observe CLI error and aborted session.

Logs (sanitized):
- auth-proxy: 2026-03-13T03:12:07Z ERROR webauthn/assertion.go:134 assertion verification failed: signature verification failed: timestamp validation failed (expected <= 5s skew, got 3720s)
- idp-sync: 2026-03-13T02:59:04Z INFO rotation-service: published new jwks to /internal/jwks (key id: rot-2026-03-13)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Install CLI v2.14.0. 2) Run `redwood ssh bastion --profile infra-usw2`. 3) Trigger WebAuthn passkey when prompted. 4) Observe assertion error and failure to obtain ephemeral SSH token.

idp-sync: 2026-03-13T02:59:04Z INFO rotation-service: published new jwks to /internal/jwks (key id: rot-2026-03-13)
cli: 2026-03-13T03:12:08Z WARN ssh-client: assertion response rejected: invalid signature/time-window
ssh-gateway: 2026-03-13T03:12:09Z INFO session-allocator: request denied: assertion timestamp outside allowed window
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token signing key rotation published a new JWKS but the auth-proxy cache did not immediately refresh, causing verification code to consult an old key or enforce a stricter timestamp window. Secondary hypothesis: some developer machines have local clocks skewed (NTP drift) combined with a change in allowed skew enforcement in auth-proxy. Evidence: logs show a large skew value (3720s ~ 62 minutes) which suggests either client timestamp is far in the future or server expects a different origin/timebase. Reproduced with a test key: toggling auth-proxy's jwks cache TTL to 0 allowed immediate retrieval of new keys and a successful assertion flow in one trial. However, multiple attempts intermittently fail indicating a race between rotation propagation and assertion validation (cache + multiple replicas of auth-proxy).
next_steps: 1) Roll back enforcement change that reduced allowed timestamp skew to previous value (temporary mitigation). 2) Increase jwks refresh concurrency and add backoff jitter to prevent cache stampedes during rotation. 3) Add healthcheck to rotation-service to notify auth-proxy replicas and invalidate caches immediately via pub/sub. 4) Ask SRE to verify NTP status across failing clients and servers. 5) Schedule follow-up to harden CLI to surface clearer error and retry once on assertion failure.
comments: Samira Gupta (2026-03-13): Reported initial outage from infra team. Attached user stderr and CLI traces. Noted that browser-based console SSO still works for same users.

Riley Martinez (2026-03-13): Assigned for investigation. I can reproduce locally after forcing a jwks rotation. Looking into auth-proxy cache TTL and replica propagation. Will coordinate with platform-sre.

Platform-SRE #oncall (2026-03-13): Confirmed auth-proxy fleet had staggered JWKS cache states; two replicas still serving old key for ~3 minutes during rotation. NTP daemons look healthy on servers; requesting list of affected client hostnames to validate user end clocks.

Harper Liu (2026-03-13): Provided a failing developer host (host-iex-02) and its `chronyc tracking` output showing ~65 seconds forward drift. We're patching NTP config on that host as part of mitigation.

Riley Martinez (2026-03-14): Deployed temporary rollback of skew enforcement at 03:30 UTC which restored CLI flow for most users. Implemented immediate jwks cache invalidation hook to reduce rotation window. Monitoring for reoccurrence.
Samira Gupta (2026-03-14): Confirmed 6/7 affected engineers can now authenticate; one user still shows failure and will be escalated if not resolved after NTP fix.
Platform-SRE (2026-03-14): Filed follow-up task INT-982022 to implement robust broadcast invalidation and add end-to-end tests for rotations.
resolution: Mitigated: temporarily relaxed timestamp-skew enforcement and pushed a cache-invalidation workaround. Ongoing: full fix scheduled (rota-broadcast + backoff) and client-side NTP drifts being corrected. Final resolution pending follow-up ticket INT-982022.
workaround: Users can temporarily use the web console or connect from a machine with corrected system clock. SRE applied a temporary change to auth-proxy to accept +/- 5 minute skew during rotation window.
